title: Transportation
content:
Transportation projects, planning, and data for Albuquerque.
This section separates long-range plans and funding from current projects, while preserving the lead agency and source date for each item. City streets, regional programs, Bernalillo County facilities, and state highways are intentionally kept distinct.
Start with Transportation Plans for the adopted regional framework and current improvement program. Use Roadway Projects, Bicycling, and Transit for mode- or corridor-specific information.

title: Development & Land Use
content:
Major development projects, development activity, zoning, land-use regulation, and the public processes that shape Albuquerque’s built environment.
This section covers significant residential, commercial, hotel, industrial, institutional, and mixed-use development without attempting to reproduce every routine permit or private filing. It also preserves the plans, regulations, data, and review standards needed to understand how projects advance.
Start with Projects for selected development activity and supporting data. For the plans that shaped neighborhoods and reinvestment, see Metropolitan Redevelopment Plans and Area & Sector Plans. For regulations and site research, see Zoning & IDO and Development Process.

title: Parks & Public Works
content:
City facilities, parks, and infrastructure projects.
This section covers City parks, facilities, and capital work, with clearly labeled County data when it provides useful regional context. It does not duplicate current project trackers; those stay linked to the agencies that maintain schedules and project attributes.
See Parks & Recreation, Stormwater & Drainage, City Facilities, and Capital Projects.

title: City Data
content:
City budget, spending, and demographic data.
Use this section for the City’s adopted budget and capital program, alongside maintained data about people, neighborhoods, public safety, climate, and environmental performance. Live datasets are linked directly to their publishers; permanent adopted records are preserved in the document library.
Start with Budget & Spending, Capital Spending, Demographics, Public Safety Data, and Climate & Environment.

title: Design References
content:
Reference drawings, engineering details, and technical guidance related to transportation infrastructure and street design.
Bernalillo County Standards#Current Bernalillo County Technical Standards Page
Provides the County’s maintained development and public-infrastructure standards, standard drawings, drainage and transportation requirements, and technical references used to review and construct improvements in unincorporated Bernalillo County.
Complete Bernalillo County Technical Standards — March 28, 2023 (archived PDF)
Contains the County’s 226-page March 2023 requirements for development review, transportation networks, road geometry, pedestrian and bicycle facilities, drainage, pavement design, traffic studies, construction, and green stormwater infrastructure.
Official County PDF
Green Stormwater Infrastructure / Low Impact Development Standards (2023 archived PDF)
Provides Bernalillo County’s design standards for desert-adapted green stormwater infrastructure and low-impact development, covering site planning, soils, vegetation, runoff, treatment practices, calculations, construction, maintenance, standard details, and application within public projects and development review.
Official County PDF · Check the current County standards page
NMDOT Quick Build Guide#Reference guidance for quick-build transportation and multimodal safety projects.
NMDOT Quick Build Guide
Introduces quick-build project planning, design, materials, public engagement, installation, and evaluation practices for delivering lower-cost multimodal safety improvements on New Mexico streets.
Toronto-Style “Tall Curbs” for Bike Lane Protection#High-profile concrete curb barriers used for physical separation and protection of bicycle lanes and other multimodal facilities.
Toronto-Style Tall Curb Engineering Drawings
Provides engineering drawings and dimensional details for the high-profile concrete curb units used to create physical separation between bicycle lanes and motor-vehicle traffic.
Tall Curb Spec Sheet
Summarizes the standard tall-curb unit’s geometry and construction specifications for designers, contractors, and reviewers planning protected bicycle-lane separation treatments on Albuquerque projects.
Tall Curb End Spec Sheet
Documents the geometry and construction requirements for terminal curb units, which provide a defined transition at the beginning or end of a tall-curb installation.
Tall Curb Full Installation Procedures
Presents the complete field-installation sequence for tall-curb barriers, including layout, pavement preparation, positioning, anchoring, and checks needed for a consistent finished installation.
Tall Curb Anchor Pin Installation Guidelines
Gives focused field guidance for installing the anchor pins that secure tall-curb units to pavement, supporting consistent placement and durable protected-lane installations.

title: Maps & Data
content:
Interactive maps, datasets, and dashboards are grouped here by tool rather than policy topic. A map may also appear in its substantive category—such as Bike Maps or Zoning & IDO—so it can be found from either direction without duplicating the source data.
Browse Maps for geographic reference tools and Dashboards for current project, safety, and program data.

title: ABQ Ride
content:
ABQ Ride bus service information and data.
Rider Information#ABQ RIDE: Routes and Schedules
The City’s current route, schedule, detour, and trip-planning information. Consult the official service page before a trip because operational details can change.
Uptown Connect#Uptown Connect Project Page
Tracks the City’s transit-centered redevelopment of the Uptown Transit Center, including design and construction progress, the transit plaza, affordable and market-rate housing, commercial space, sustainability features, and the anticipated 2026–2028 delivery schedule.
ABQ RIDE Forward Network Plan#Official ABQ RIDE Forward Project Page
Tracks the finalized bus-network plan, phased implementation, current project status, official reports, route concepts, and project contact information maintained by the City.
Final Recovery Network Plan (June 2025)
Defines the finalized route network, frequencies, service spans, access changes, public-input response, and phased next steps for rebuilding and modernizing Albuquerque bus service. Official City PDF
Final Recovery Network Map (2025)
Maps the finalized ABQ RIDE Forward network by route and frequency, providing a printable overview of planned fixed-route service and demand-response areas. Official City image
Planning History#Phase III Recovery Network Report (May 2024)
Presents the draft recovery network, proposed route and frequency changes, service assumptions, access analysis, demographic outcomes, and recommendations later refined into the final plan. Official City PDF
Phase III Engagement Summary (November 2024)
Documents community and stakeholder feedback on the draft recovery network, including outreach, survey results, route-specific comments, respondent characteristics, and requested changes. Official City PDF
Phase II Concepts Report (March 2023)
Compares contrasting high-ridership and high-coverage bus-network concepts, explaining route structures, service tradeoffs, access outcomes, transit markets, and choices considered during redesign. Official City PDF
Phase II Engagement Summary (August 2023)
Summarizes public preferences between high-ridership and high-coverage concepts, including surveys, focus groups, stakeholder input, demographic analysis, and priorities for evening and weekend service. Official City PDF
Phase I Existing Conditions Report (August 2022)
Analyzes Albuquerque transit markets, network and route performance, ridership, service frequency, access, equity, zero fares, worker shortages, and fundamental network-design choices. Official City PDF
Phase I Engagement Summary (February 2023)
Records early community priorities and transit tradeoffs gathered through surveys, focus groups, pop-up events, workshops, meetings, presentations, and outreach to riders and underserved populations. Official City PDF
2022 ABQ RIDE On-Board Rider Survey
Profiles weekday and weekend riders, travel patterns, transfers, trip purposes, service use, demographics, automobile access, and priorities for improving Albuquerque bus service, providing the rider baseline used during ABQ RIDE Forward and later zero-fare policy analysis. City resolution citing the original survey
Project contact: Andrew de Garmo, Principal Planner, ABQ RIDE — adegarmo@cabq.gov — 505-724-3109.
Montaño Intermodal Center Planning History#Montaño Intermodal Center Project Application (2010 archived PDF)
Documents the City’s federal funding application for a Montaño intermodal center, connecting Rail Runner, local bus service, walking, bicycling, housing, employment, neighborhood access, and coordinated transportation investment.
Official City PDF · Official City transit document collection
Earlier Transit Investment Studies#Albuquerque Streetcar Evaluation Summary Report (2008 archived PDF)
Evaluates a proposed modern streetcar through Albuquerque’s historic and cultural core, examining ridership, operations, costs, land-use and economic-development benefits, funding, implementation, and comparisons with peer systems.
Official City PDF
Albuquerque Streetcar Evaluation Appendices (2008 archived PDF)
Preserves the streetcar evaluation’s supporting technical record, including peer systems, operating costs, ridership, preliminary cost analysis, land-use benefits, funding analysis, earlier HDR work, and the February 2008 introductory presentation.
Official City PDF
Albuquerque Streetcar Cost and Ridership Analysis (2008 archived PDF)
Reviews the proposed Albuquerque modern streetcar’s capital and operating costs, ridership assumptions, peer systems, service design, land-use forecasts, and potential development impacts as the baseline for the broader 2008 rail-investment evaluation.
Official City PDF · Official City project archive
Open Data#ABQ RIDE Open Data
The City publishes General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) data for applications and analysis. The live feed is preferable to an archived copy for current service information.

title: Area & Sector Plans
content:
Historical area, sector, and community plans that explain how Albuquerque neighborhoods, infrastructure, land use, and transportation developed. Many no longer control zoning, but remain important planning-history records.
City Area & Sector Development Plan Library
Maintains the City’s current reference index for adopted historical plans. ABQInfo preserves selected complete plans and adoption records whose context remains independently useful.
Southwest Mesa and Volcano Area#Southwest Area Plan (Bernalillo County 2001; Albuquerque 2002)
Preserves the jointly adopted Southwest Area Plan covering growth, land use, transportation, infrastructure, community form, environmental resources, public facilities, economic development, implementation, and City and County responsibilities.
Official City plan library · Official City PDF
Volcano Trails Sector Development Plan (2011)
Preserves the adopted Volcano Trails framework for village-center and residential development, open space, transportation, trails, infrastructure, urban design, zoning, implementation, and protection of the volcanic landscape.
Official City plan library · Official City PDF
Volcano Trails Sector Development Plan Adoption Resolution R-11-211 (2011)
Records City Council’s adoption and zoning actions for the 446-acre Volcano Trails plan area, including village center, residential districts, open space, boundaries, findings, and implementation conditions.
Official City project archive · Official City PDF
Fourth Street and Montaño#Fourth Street and Montaño Community Visioning Report (2004)
Documents community priorities for the Fourth Street and Montaño area, including traffic, pedestrian safety, drainage, neighborhood character, commercial development, public space, land use, and coordinated improvement strategies.
Official City project archive · Official City PDF

title: Bicycling
content:
Bicycle infrastructure, planning, and safety data.
The bicycle section distinguishes system plans and mapped facilities from individual projects. The Projects page groups recent work from 2021 forward under Current Projects and older records under Past Projects.
Start with Projects for individual investments, Bike Plans for the network framework, Bike Maps for live geographic tools, and Safety & Crash Data for City and regional safety sources.
Laws and Operating Rules#Albuquerque Bike Laws
Connects riders to Albuquerque and New Mexico bicycle laws, safety and rights information, and the City’s current electric-bicycle map, classifications, operating rules, and frequently asked questions.

title: Bike Maps
content:
Multi-use trails and paths in Albuquerque.
City Bicycle Maps#Albuquerque Bike Maps
Provides the current Albuquerque Bicycle and Trail Map, the City’s interactive bicycle map, facility-type guidance, trail-riding guides, and public-art bicycle tours, plus locations where printed maps are available.
Albuquerque Bikeways and Trails Map (2026 archived PDF)
Preserves the City’s 2026 printable bikeways and trails map, showing bicycle boulevards, bike lanes, separated facilities, paved and unpaved trails, transit connections, services, destinations, and riding guidance across Albuquerque.
Official City PDF · Check for the current City map
50-Mile Activity Loop Map (2020 archived PDF)
Maps Albuquerque’s signed 50-Mile Activity Loop and alternate routes, identifying completed and pending segments, trail and street connections, construction detours, major destinations, transit links, and the route through Downtown, the Bosque, foothills, and West Side.
Official City PDF · Official City project page
Bikeways and Trails Public Map Viewer
Maps Albuquerque’s currently maintained bikeways and trails by facility type, providing a searchable public view of bike lanes, separated facilities, bicycle boulevards, sidepaths, and multi-use trails.
Proposed Bike Network
Maps Albuquerque’s existing and proposed bicycle infrastructure together, allowing users to explore planned connections and compare the future network with facilities already in place.
Current Bikeways and Trails Data
Publishes the City’s actively maintained bikeway and trail data layer, distinguishing current infrastructure from the static network snapshot used to develop the 2024 facilities plan.
City Trail Guides#Bicycle Boulevard Guide — Full Version (2020 archived PDF)
Provides a detailed guided bicycle tour of Albuquerque’s Bicycle Boulevard, combining turn-by-turn navigation with neighborhood history, architecture, public art, natural features, cultural sites, optional side trips, parking guidance, and transit access.
Official City PDF
Paseo del Bosque Trail Guide — Full Version (2020 archived PDF)
Guides riders along the Paseo del Bosque Trail with route directions, parking and transit access, distances, side trips, natural history, cultural sites, public art, neighborhood context, and connections across Albuquerque’s river corridor.
Official City PDF
I-40 Trail Guide — Full Version (2020 archived PDF)
Guides riders along Albuquerque’s I-40 bicycle trail and parallel street connections, with route directions, parking, transit access, neighborhood history, public art, cultural destinations, natural features, and optional side trips from the West Side to Tramway.
Official City PDF
Tramway Trail Guide — Full Version (2020 archived PDF)
Guides a 16-mile ride along Tramway Boulevard and connected trails, combining navigation, parking and transit access, Sandia foothills geology and wildlife, local history, public art, cultural sites, and side trips between Central Avenue and North Fourth Street.
Official City PDF · Check for current City trail guides
Unser Boulevard, Mariposa, and Riverview Trail Guide (archived PDF)
Provides a detailed West Side bicycle tour with route maps, trail connections, parking, transit access, mileage, neighborhood history, landscape, geology, public art, and points of interest.
Official City PDF · Check for current City trail guides
Northeast Heights Bike Trails Guide (2020 archived PDF)
Connects six major Northeast Heights trail corridors with route narratives, maps, street links, distances, access guidance, landscape history, public spaces, and practical notes for cross-city bicycle trips.
Official City PDF · Check for current City trail guides
Paseo de las Montañas Trail Guide (2020 archived PDF)
Guides riders along the Piedra Lisa and Embudo arroyo trails with maps, parking, mileage, connections, neighborhood architecture, geology, hydrology, natural history, parks, and public art.
Official City PDF · Check for current City trail guides
Regional Long-Range Bikeway Network#MRMPO Active Transportation Map Portfolio
Opens MRMPO’s maintained active-transportation portfolio, updated in 2026, with interactive long-range bikeway and bicycle traffic-stress resources for exploring regional network conditions and planned connections.
Pedestrian Level of Traffic Stress Map
Maps relative pedestrian comfort along Albuquerque-area roads using factors such as traffic volume, speed, roadway configuration, and sidewalk conditions, helping identify corridors where walking improvements may be needed.
MRMPO Long-Range Bikeway System Map (2026)
Maps the adopted long-range bikeway network for the Albuquerque metropolitan planning area, distinguishing existing and proposed regional bicycle facilities used to guide coordination, project development, and future investment.
County GIS Data#Bernalillo County Bikeways
This live Bernalillo County GIS service maps county-maintained bikeways in unincorporated Bernalillo County. Use it as a current reference for facilities beyond Albuquerque city limits; the county publishes it as data, not a static map.
Bernalillo County Multi-Use Trails
This live Bernalillo County GIS service maps county-maintained multi-use trails in unincorporated areas. Motorized traffic is excluded from these trails, making the service a useful companion to local bicycle and pedestrian network maps.
MRMPO Bicycle and Pedestrian Planning Maps
Collects regional pedestrian-priority, pedestrian traffic-stress, long-range bikeway, and bicycle traffic-stress maps used to identify needs and guide active-transportation planning across the Albuquerque metropolitan area.

title: Bike Plans
content:
City bicycle planning documents and master plans, including current and previous network plans and supporting materials.
Current Bike Plan#2024 Bikeway and Trail Facilities Plan
Establishes Albuquerque’s current bicycle and trail network vision, policies, facility recommendations, project priorities, and implementation framework for safer, better-connected active transportation.
Combined City Edition (Main Plan and Appendices)
Preserves the City’s complete 513-page publication in one file, combining the adopted plan with the crossings guide and appendices for convenient archival reference. Official City PDF
Bicycle and Trail Crossings Guide
Provides design guidance for bicycle and trail crossings, helping practitioners select treatments that improve visibility, clarify priority, and reduce conflicts at roadway intersections.
Appendix A – Planning and Policy Framework
Summarizes the adopted plans, policies, and regulatory context that shaped the 2024 plan’s goals, network recommendations, priorities, and implementation approach.
Appendix B – Community Survey Summary (Spring 2023)
Reports responses from the spring 2023 community survey, documenting residents’ bicycling and trail experiences, concerns, priorities, and desired improvements across Albuquerque.
Appendix C – Project Priorities Survey Map Results (Fall 2023)
Compiles mapped results from the fall 2023 priorities survey, showing where participants identified desired bikeway, crossing, connection, and trail improvements.
Appendix D – Bikeway Evaluation Process
Explains the plan’s repeatable method for evaluating proposed bikeways, comparing corridor conditions, network needs, feasibility, and project priorities across Albuquerque.
Appendix E – Bike Boulevard Toolkit
Describes planning and design tools for low-stress bicycle boulevards, including traffic calming, crossing improvements, wayfinding, and strategies for managing motor-vehicle volumes.
Appendix F – Priority Projects Tables (Jan 2025)
Lists the plan’s priority bicycle and trail projects as of January 2025, organizing recommended improvements for implementation and future programming.
Appendix G – Project Profiles
Presents detailed profiles for selected priority projects, describing corridor needs, recommended facilities, implementation considerations, and each project’s role in the network.
Appendix H – Multiuse Trail Considerations (2015 Plan)
Preserves relevant multiuse-trail planning and design considerations from the 2015 plan for continued technical reference alongside the updated 2024 recommendations.
Appendix I – Bollard Assessment (2013)
Documents the City’s 2013 assessment of multiuse-trail bollards, including operational and safety considerations that inform decisions about access-control treatments on trails.
Interactive Plan Companions#Bikeways & Trails 2024 Conditions
Explains the existing-condition analysis behind Albuquerque’s 2024 Bikeway and Trail Facilities Plan, including facility gaps, bicycle traffic stress, comfort, equity, Vision Zero, and underlying interactive data.
Existing & Proposed Network
Presents the existing and proposed bikeway network supporting Albuquerque’s adopted 2024 plan, linking interactive maps with project strategies, prioritization, and the plan’s broader recommendations.
Previous Bike Plans#2015 Bikeways and Trails Facilities Plan
The previous adopted facilities plan established the bicycle and trail network, policies, design guidance, and project priorities that preceded the current 2024 plan.
Appendix A: Proposed Facilities
Preserves the 2015 plan’s detailed proposed-facilities tables, listing bikeways and trails by facility type, street or route, endpoints, priority category, length, and project status for historical network comparison. Official City PDF
2011 Albuquerque Bikeways and Trails Master Plan Update
Updated Albuquerque’s earlier bicycle and trail planning framework, documenting existing conditions, proposed networks, facility guidance, and implementation priorities at that time.
Appendices
Preserves the plan’s needs analysis, bicycle counts, survey findings, crash analysis, Safe Routes to School material, public-meeting records, and other supporting research. Official City PDF
Design Guidelines
Documents Albuquerque-specific guidance for bikeways, trails, intersections, crossings, wayfinding, site design, and innovative treatments developed alongside the 2011 plan update. Official City PDF
2000 Albuquerque Comprehensive On-Street Bicycle Plan
Established a citywide framework for Albuquerque’s on-street bicycle facilities, identifying network needs, recommended routes, design approaches, policies, and implementation priorities.
1993 Trails and Bikeways Facility Plan
Documents Albuquerque’s early citywide approach to developing connected trail and bikeway facilities, preserving the historical basis for subsequent network planning.
Related Bicycle Policy#City Council Resolution R-07-268: Bike Boulevards (2007)
Designates Mountain Road, Silver Avenue, and 14th Street bike-boulevard routes; appropriates up to $400,000 for design, engineering, and initial implementation; and directs amendments to the Comprehensive Bikeway Facilities Plan.

title: Budget & Spending
content:
City budget and expenditure data.
Current Budget#City of Albuquerque Approved Budget, Fiscal Year 2027
The City of Albuquerque’s adopted Fiscal Year 2027 budget provides citywide revenue, appropriations, department and program details, capital support, performance information, and summary charts explaining where public funds come from and how they are allocated.

title: Capital Projects
content:
Public works capital improvement projects.
Current Project Data#City Council Current, Neighborhood, and Completed Projects
Opens the Council’s unusually useful project archive, which organizes current initiatives, district and neighborhood capital work, completed studies, reports, corridor plans, task-force records, and supporting documents.
Municipal Development Featured Projects
The City’s maintained index highlights major transportation, facility, safety, parks, and public-space capital projects, providing an accessible project gateway while the machine-readable project-data endpoint is unavailable.
DMD Active Projects Viewer
Maps active and completed Municipal Development projects by phase, category, district, and location, with searchable descriptions covering transportation, traffic engineering, drainage, facilities, and other special projects.
Historical Project Snapshots#DMD 2025 Project Highlights
Preserves an interactive snapshot of DMD’s 2025 streetlight, roadway, neighborhood traffic management, bicycle, and pedestrian projects, making the year’s highlighted work easier to explore geographically.
2025 General Obligation Bond Approved Program Book
The City’s adopted bond program is cataloged in City Data and is cross-linked here because it is an important source of public-works capital funding. The document is stored once, not duplicated.

title: Capital Spending
content:
Capital improvement spending and projects.
Capital Program#2025 General Obligation Bond Approved Program Book
Albuquerque’s approved 2025 General Obligation Bond program describes proposed capital investments across the 2025-2034 decade plan, including project scopes, funding categories, public facilities, infrastructure, and implementation priorities.

title: City Facilities
content:
City buildings and facilities.
Public-Facility References#Accessible City Park and Recreation Facilities
The City identifies accessible parks, recreation facilities, and programs, with an accompanying location map. It is a maintained public-facing resource rather than a static facilities inventory.

title: Climate & Environment
content:
City and regional climate plans, greenhouse-gas inventories, and durable performance records relevant to Albuquerque.
City Climate Action Plan and Implementation Hub
Maintains Albuquerque’s current climate-plan overview, implementation reports, inventories, updates, and related Sustainability Office work. Archived records below preserve the planning lineage and measured baseline.
Climate Action Plans#City of Albuquerque Climate Action Plan (2009)
Preserves Albuquerque’s first Climate Action Task Force recommendations, covering greenhouse-gas accounting, buildings, renewable energy, neighborhoods, food, waste, behavior change, and transportation before the City’s later equity-centered plan.
Official City climate-plan hub · Official City PDF
Albuquerque Climate Action Plan (2021)
Sets Albuquerque’s community-scale climate strategy with equity-centered actions for governance, energy, buildings, transportation, waste, economic development, adaptation, health, and accountability, informed by frontline-community engagement and implementation priorities.
Official City climate-plan hub · Official City PDF
Greenhouse-Gas Inventory#Central New Mexico Community-Scale Greenhouse Gas Inventory (2023)
Quantifies 2023 community greenhouse-gas emissions across Central New Mexico, documenting methods, energy, transportation, waste, industrial sources, agriculture, land use, and the baseline used for regional climate planning and progress measurement.
Official City climate-plan hub · Official City PDF

title: Dashboards
content:
Data dashboards and visualizations.
Project, Program, and Safety Dashboards#DMD Active Projects Viewer
Maps active and completed Municipal Development projects by phase, category, district, and location, with searchable descriptions covering transportation, traffic engineering, drainage, facilities, and other special projects.
DMD by the Numbers
Summarizes the infrastructure assets maintained by Albuquerque’s Department of Municipal Development, providing a high-level operational inventory across streets, signals, lighting, drainage, and related systems.
Street Maintenance Projects Viewer
Maps City street-maintenance projects and their locations, providing a direct geographic view of active and recent resurfacing or maintenance work managed by Municipal Development.
Streetlight Status Dashboard
Displays weekly updated operational status for City streetlights using vendor data, helping users examine working and non-working assets while the City expands integration with PNM work-order information.
School Crossings Dashboard
Maps and rates more than 350 Albuquerque school crossings, with filters for schools, areas, and crossing features; ratings were updated in 2024 and are maintained as conditions change.
Neighborhood Traffic Management Program Dashboard
Maps eligible Neighborhood Traffic Management Program streets and current requests, with searchable request IDs, dates, locations, project status, and filters for tracking neighborhood traffic-calming activity.
Permitted Construction in the Public Right of Way
The City’s regularly updated map shows permitted right-of-way construction, locations, dates, descriptions, and responsible contractors. It is cross-listed under Current Roadway Projects for people tracking active work.
Open the Live Traffic Barricades Map.
Construction Moratoriums
Maps current event and seasonal construction restrictions, affected street boundaries, and effective dates. It is cross-listed under Current Roadway Projects because the restrictions directly affect construction scheduling.
Pedestrian, Bicyclist, and Traffic-Safety Projects Map
This City map points to the current geographic view of safety projects. It is also linked from the bicycle-safety section because the same live source serves both purposes.
Open the Live Project Viewer.
NMDOT Project Dashboard
NMDOT’s statewide dashboard is useful for tracking state highway work affecting Albuquerque. Use the accompanying project pages for the record of a particular study or corridor.
NMDOT STIP Viewer
The Statewide Transportation Improvement Program viewer is the current source for programmed transportation projects. It complements, but does not replace, the regional MRCOG Transportation Improvement Program.
MRMPO TIP Viewer
Searches the active regional Transportation Improvement Program by project, agency, location, funding, and programmed year. Use it to inspect current Albuquerque-area roadway, transit, bicycle, pedestrian, and safety investments and revisions beyond the static archived TIP document.
NMDOT Active Projects
Maps state transportation projects in study, design, and construction, including major Albuquerque work, and provides project descriptions, development phases, public-meeting information, and links to dedicated project resources.
MRCOG Traffic Flow Maps and Busiest Intersections
MRCOG provides current and historical regional traffic counts, annual weekday traffic maps, vehicle-miles-traveled information, and an interactive traffic-flow map for the Albuquerque metropolitan planning area.
Transportation Analysis and Querying Application
Provides public access to MRMPO travel-time, traffic-count, and volume-to-capacity data, with geographic and time-based queries supporting corridor analysis, congestion comparison, infrastructure planning, and project development.
MRCOG Traffic Counts Viewer
Maps regional traffic counts by roadway section and approximate count location, with tabular-data and map exports supporting analysis across Albuquerque, Bernalillo County, and the wider MRCOG planning area.
High Fatal and Injury Network
Maps five years of fatal and injury crashes to identify Albuquerque-area streets and intersections with above-average risk, including pedestrian and bicycle crashes, while noting that each location requires further engineering study.
Road Diet Candidates Map
Presents MRMPO’s 2023 screening of roadways that may support safety-focused reconfiguration based on lanes, capacity, and traffic volume. Candidate status is preliminary and does not replace project-specific engineering analysis.

title: Demographics
content:
Albuquerque demographic and census data.
Regional Data#MRCOG Socioeconomic Data
Mid-Region Council of Governments publishes regional population, households, employment, income, commuting, and related planning data. It is the appropriate regional source when a question extends beyond City limits.
Albuquerque Neighborhood Data
The City’s open-data service provides neighborhood geography and associated data resources for map-based analysis, local reference, and comparisons among Albuquerque communities.
MRCOG Community Profiles
Summarizes the central New Mexico region’s population, geography, counties, municipalities, pueblos, transportation connections, and urban-rural context, providing a concise companion to detailed census and socioeconomic datasets.

title: Development Process
content:
Cross-cutting development process documents, manuals, and reference materials.
Development Process Manual#Development Process Manual (June 2, 2020)
Provides the City’s technical requirements and procedures for planning, designing, reviewing, permitting, and constructing public infrastructure associated with development projects.
County Development Review#Bernalillo County Traffic Impact Analysis
Explains when development in unincorporated Bernalillo County requires transportation-impact analysis and connects applicants to the County’s review process, technical expectations, transportation planning, and development standards.
Infrastructure Financing#Albuquerque Public Improvement Districts
Explains how Albuquerque creates and governs public improvement districts to finance streets, trails, utilities, parks, public buildings, and other infrastructure through property taxes, assessments, bonds, petitions, hearings, and elections.

title: Maps
content:
Interactive maps of city data and infrastructure.
Citywide Reference Maps#Regional Long-Range Transportation Maps#Albuquerque Metropolitan Planning Area Boundary Map (2020)
Maps the official Albuquerque Metropolitan Planning Area boundary and member jurisdictions used for federally required metropolitan transportation planning, programming, data analysis, and regional coordination.
MRMPO Bikeway System Map (2026)
MRMPO Pedestrian System Map (2026)
MRMPO Roadway System Map (2026)
MRMPO Transit System Map (2026)
These adopted regional maps show the existing and proposed long-range networks used by MRMPO to coordinate bicycle, pedestrian, roadway, and transit planning across the Albuquerque metropolitan area.
Interactive Long Range Roadway System Map
Provides an interactive view of MRMPO’s Long Range Roadway System using May 2026 data, complementing the adopted printable map with searchable geography and roadway details across the metropolitan planning area.
Historical Transportation Maps#2040 Long-Range Roadway Map
Preserves the City’s earlier 2040 roadway planning map, showing long-range functional classifications and network connections for comparison with current regional roadway-system guidance.
Official City Transportation Development Section · Official City PDF
City Maps for the Public
The City’s map library includes the official Zone Atlas, address and parcel reference tools, council districts, land use, streets, neighborhoods, and printable maps.
Council District Poster Map — January 2026 (archived PDF)
Provides the City’s January 2026 printable council-district map with district boundaries and councilor photographs, offering a dated civic-reference snapshot for preservation alongside the live council map.
View the official CABQ ArcGIS item and check for updates.
Open Space Maps
Albuquerque Open Space maintains access and trail maps for its lands and trailheads. Individual trail maps are available from the same City source when a printable field reference is useful.
Archived Open Space Maps and Guides#Paseo de la Mesa Recreation Trail Map (2018)
Maps the recreation trail, parking, adjoining Major Public Open Space and Petroglyph National Monument lands, nearby volcanic features, streets, and Northwest Mesa connections.
Sandia Foothills Open Space Trail Map (Revised 2006)
Preserves a dated field map of the foothills trail network, trailheads, numbered routes, Elena Gallegos, Embudito, Bear Canyon, access streets, and Wilderness boundary.
City of Albuquerque Open Space Overview Map
Provides a systemwide reference to City Open Space properties and nearby tribal, federal, county, and municipal lands across the Bosque, foothills, volcanic mesa, and East Mountain areas.
Albuquerque Bird Watching Guide and Map (2019)
Maps Albuquerque birding locations and connects them with habitat and species guidance for the Bosque, wetlands, foothills, parks, Open Space lands, and accessible urban wildlife-viewing sites.
Los Poblanos Fields Open Space Trail Map (2020)
Maps trails, access points, parking, agricultural fields, drains, nearby streets, and route distances around the Rio Grande Community Farm and Agri-Nature Center.
Open Space Visitor Center and Bosque Trail Access Map
Maps the Visitor Center property, parking, river loop, Bosque canopy loop, agricultural fields, viewing area, nearby drains, and connections toward Montaño and Paseo del Norte.

title: Traffic Operations
content:
Regional roadway operations, traffic analysis, incident management, and intelligent transportation systems.
City Street Operations#Albuquerque Area Street Jurisdictions
Identifies whether Albuquerque-area public streets are maintained by the City, Bernalillo County, NMDOT, or another entity, with address search and jurisdiction boundaries.
Interstate Maintenance Responsibilities
Maps litter, debris, and landscape-maintenance responsibilities along Albuquerque interstates and freeways, helping users distinguish City, NMDOT, and other operational roles.
City Street Speed-Limit Data
Publishes Albuquerque street speed-limit data as a live GIS service derived from OpenStreetMap, supporting mapping and analysis while requiring users to consider the source’s stated limitations.
Street Maintenance Projects Viewer
Maps City street-maintenance projects and their locations, providing a direct geographic view of active and recent resurfacing or maintenance work managed by Municipal Development.
Streetlight Status Dashboard
Displays weekly updated operational status for City streetlights using vendor data, helping users examine working and non-working assets while the City expands integration with PNM work-order information.
Bernalillo County Street Operations#Street Maintenance
Explains Bernalillo County’s roadway-maintenance responsibilities and service requests for pavement, potholes, grading, signs, striping, vegetation, snow response, and related conditions in unincorporated areas.
Traffic Engineering
Describes County traffic-engineering services for signals, signs, markings, speed studies, traffic counts, safety evaluations, school zones, and requests affecting streets outside Albuquerque’s municipal maintenance jurisdiction.
Traffic Analysis#MRCOG Traffic Counts Viewer
Maps regional traffic counts by roadway section and approximate count location, with tabular-data and map exports supporting analysis across Albuquerque, Bernalillo County, and the wider MRCOG planning area.
MRMPO Traffic Monitoring
Explains MRMPO’s regional traffic-count program and links roadway volumes, vehicle classifications, speeds, flow maps, and related tools used to understand Albuquerque-area travel patterns, congestion, and infrastructure needs.
Congestion Management Process Archives
Preserves regional corridor rankings, congestion profiles, strategy matrices, network maps, commuting studies, transit travel-time analysis, adaptive-signal findings, and related Albuquerque-area congestion-management work dating to 2008.

Collects regional plans, maps, strategies, and incident-management resources for coordinated traffic signals, traveler information, dynamic message signs, roadway monitoring, emergency response, and other technology-based transportation operations.

Defines the regional framework and consensus blueprint for coordinated intelligent transportation system deployment, data sharing, project phasing, federal compliance, and consistency with metropolitan plans and programmed projects.
FFY 2024-2029 TIP ITS Review and Architecture Certification (2023)
Documents MRMPO’s review of 56 proposed transportation projects, identifying 33 with intelligent-system elements and certifying their alignment with regional service packages, federal architecture rules, and systems-engineering requirements.

title: Transportation Plans
content:
Regional plans, long-range plans, and other system-level transportation planning documents.

Establishes the Albuquerque metropolitan area’s adopted long-range transportation vision through 2045, including regional growth assumptions, multimodal needs, safety and equity goals, funded projects, performance measures, and implementation priorities.

Preserves the plan’s complete supporting appendix, including technical methods, demographic and travel forecasts, project evaluation, public and agency input, environmental analysis, financial assumptions, and federally required documentation.

Summarizes the adopted metropolitan plan’s regional trends, goals, multimodal investment strategy, safety and equity approach, project priorities, environmental resilience, and implementation framework through the 2045 planning horizon.

PDF oficial de MRCOG

Preserves earlier Albuquerque metropolitan transportation plans, chapters, appendices, project lists, financial analyses, performance measures, environmental-resilience work, public outreach, and long-range system guidance from the 2030 through 2040 cycles.

Documents public engagement conducted from 2023 through the plan’s April 2025 adoption, links the participation plan, explains how feedback informed the MTP, and provides current presentation and engagement contacts.
